sections.title: Case Presentation
sections.content: A 38-year-old man with no previous ocular history reports irritation of his right eye after doing some work around the house. On exam, the patient has 20/20 vision and normal intraocular pressure. The appearance of the anterior segment is shown above. Q1. What abnormality is present, and what is the likely cause? Q2. How would you work up this patient? Q3. How are foreign bodies classified? Q4. What findings are seen in chalcosis and siderosis? Q5. How would you treat this patient? A1: Colour anterior segment photograph focused on Iris shows iridotomy, with no past ocular history possibility of an IOFB is more likely the culprit although, no corneal opacity or entry site can be seen in this photograph.

sections.title: Clinical Investigation & Workup
content: History: Detailed inquiry regarding work type (hammering, sawing, power tools).
Protection: Determine if eye protection was used.
Sensation: Did the patient feel a 'hit' or 'poke' to the eye?
Imaging: Orbital CT, B-scan, or X-ray.
Caution: DO NOT perform MRI if a metallic IOFB is suspected.

rows: Sunflower cataract, Kayser–Fleisher ring, green iris, sluggish pupil, retinal degeneration.
Iris heterochromia, mid-dilated pupil, lens brown-orange dots, vitritis, pigmentary RPE degeneration.
Both conditions present with reduced or absent ERG response.

branches: Inert (Glass, plastic, sand, stone, ceramic, gold, platinum, silver, aluminum - No removal required)
Reactive: Copper (<70% inert, <85% chalcosis, >85% severe endophthalmitis)

sections.title: Red Flags & Management Priorities
content: Reactive FB material MUST be surgically removed as soon as possible.
MRI is strictly contraindicated if metal is suspected.
If rural setting or wood involvement is suspected, initiate antifungal prophylaxis.

sections.title: Antibiotic Prophylaxis Protocol
content: Systemic IV: Vancomycin (1g BD) or Cefazolin (1g TDS).
Systemic IV: Ceftazidime (1g BD) for endophthalmitis coverage.
Clinical Pearl: Prophylaxis is controversial but standardly performed to mitigate endophthalmitis risk.
